title: A Salt for the Sigil
premise: Hazel Eriksen, a royal food-taster whose body is a ledger of accumulated poisons, secretly keeps the accounts of the Gild of Impossible Things, which trades in favors, memories, and miracles. When the old gods resume answering prayers, the court's new inquisitor begins hunting anyone touched by divinity—including Hazel's beloved, Wren, whose soul was sold years ago to the court beneath the mountain to pay a debt Hazel unknowingly incurred. To save Wren, Hazel must forge an entry in the gods' own ledger, trading their hard-won immunity and their invisibility for a soul the mountain refuses to release. In the end, Hazel wins Wren back at the cost of their protected anonymity, choosing to stand openly as the guild's keeper—and as someone who belongs to another person rather than to an institution.
about_author: Lior Voss is the pen name of a former line cook turned archivist who claims the best fantasy is written by people who have worked service jobs. They live near a fjord with two opinionated cats and a growing collection of antique account books.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. We open on a banquet where Hazel sips arsenic-laced wine without flinching, cataloguing flavors like scripture. Between courses they slip notes into the guild's hidden ledger. The beat: competence masking loneliness—Hazel is valued only as a vessel that can die safely.

chapters.title: Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At night, Hazel balances the guild's books: a widow's borrowed luck, a soldier's returned courage. Their handler, Magpie, explains the old rule—the guild survives by being unrecorded. The beat: warmth found in secret work, shadowed by the warning that visibility means death.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, a lamplighter, prays half-jokingly to a forgotten river god—and the god answers, lighting every lamp in the district at once. Wren hides the miracle but feels seen for the first time. The beat: wonder tangled with immediate fear of the inquisitor's patrols.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Question
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Inquisitor Serane Vail arrives at court, elegant and terrifying, asking about 'unlicensed divinity.' She tastes-test Hazel herself, probing what poisons haven't killed them. The beat: cat-and-mouse tension; Hazel realizes their immunity reads, to Serane, like a miracle.

chapters.title: What Wren Sold
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Digging through old guild entries, Hazel finds the truth: Wren's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain to settle a debt from Hazel's own apprenticeship—a trade Hazel signed without reading. The beat: guilt detonating quietly; love reframed as obligation.

chapters.title: Salt and Signature
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts Hazel, not with anger but grief: they always knew something of them had been pawned. Together they decide to steal it back rather than buy it, because the mountain doesn't sell. The beat: fragile reconciliation; duty to each other over duty to rules.

chapters.title: The Guild Objects
chapters.summary: Magpie's POV. The guild council votes against the theft—an open act would expose centuries of invisibility. Magpie abstains, torn between the institution that saved them and the two fools it raised. The beat: institutional loyalty cracking under personal love.

chapters.title: Serane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. We see her method: she cross-references answered prayers like debts, closing in on the lamplighter district. She interrogates a priest who gives up nothing but dies anyway. The beat: chilling competence; the antagonist believes she is delivering justice, not cruelty.

chapters.title: Down the Stair Under the Root
chapters.summary: Hazel and Wren's POV, alternating. Guided by a bribed ferryman of the dead, they descend toward the mountain court through root-tunnels where prayers pool like groundwater. The beat: intimacy under pressure—each confession a step deeper.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The subterranean court is a bureaucracy of the dead: souls filed like grain, judges who speak only in contracts. Hazel poses as an auditor. The beat: uncanny dread laced with dark comedy—death run like a customs house.

chapters.title: An Entry in the Gods' Book
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel finds the master ledger of the old gods and discovers their own name written as collateral since childhood. Every poison survived was a payment collected. The beat: devastating revelation—Hazel's whole life has been someone else's amortization schedule.

chapters.title: The Price of Immunity
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A minor god offers a deal: Wren's soul for Hazel's accumulated immunities, poured out like wine. Wren nearly accepts alone. The beat: love against self-sacrifice—Wren must choose between being saved and saving Hazel from the cost.

chapters.title: Caught Between Courts
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. Serane follows them below, having traced the guild's ledger ink. She offers Hazel immunity from prosecution in exchange for the guild's books. The beat: temptation framed as mercy; the law offering safety at the price of everyone Hazel protects.

chapters.title: Forgery
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Back above ground, Hazel commits the guild's cardinal sin: forging an entry in the gods' ledger, writing Wren's soul back into Wren's body. The act requires naming themselves as guarantor. The beat: transgression as devotion—justice made by hand, outside all law.

chapters.title: The Mountain Notices
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The forgery ripples: lamps gutter citywide, the dead stir, and the mountain court dispatches collectors. Magpie burns part of the guild archive to hide Hazel's trail. The beat: consequences cascading; allies paying real costs.

chapters.title: Trial by Taste
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Serane arrests Hazel publicly and forces a trial by ordeal: a cup of every poison Hazel has ever survived, compounded. If the gods favor the forgery, Hazel lives. The beat: public reckoning—Hazel's invisibility ends before the whole court.

chapters.title: What the Old Gods Want
chapters.summary: River-god POV (brief) and Hazel's POV. The ordeal becomes communion: the old gods, starved of believers, reveal they let the sale happen to force someone brave enough to rewrite the terms. The beat: horrifying divine pragmatism met with human defiance.

chapters.title: The Cup
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel drinks. The poisons find no purchase—not because of immunity, but because the gods honor the forged signature. Hazel collapses anyway, emptied of every protection they ever built. The beat: climax—victory purchased with total vulnerability.

chapters.title: Soul Returned
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren wakes whole, feeling edges they never knew were missing, and fights through the collapsing courtroom to reach Hazel's body. The beat: desperate tenderness; belonging proven by action, not declaration.

chapters.title: Terms Renegotiated
chapters.summary: Hazel and Serane's POV. Hazel, alive but mortal as any cook, negotiates with both courts: the guild goes on record, regulated but legal, and Serane—outmaneuvered and quietly relieved—accepts. The beat: justice remade as contract rather than conquest.

chapters.title: A Name in the Book
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel writes the guild's first honest entry: their own name, beside Wren's, listed not as assets or debts but as witnesses to each other. Magpie weeps over the ledger. The beat: quiet catharsis—accounting transformed into testimony.

chapters.title: First Course
chapters.summary: Hazel and Wren's POV, shared. Months later, Hazel cooks a meal with no poisons in it and tastes nothing dangerous for the first time in their life. Above the table, a lamp flickers in answer to no prayer at all. The beat: resolution—ordinary love, chosen and visible, seasoned with a little lingering grace.
